title: Injective resolutions of a short exact sequence of bounded below complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian]. Let $0\to A^\bullet\xrightarrow{f}B^\bullet\xrightarrow{g}C^\bullet\to0$ be a sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ with $A^n=B^n=C^n=0$ for $n<0$ which is short exact in each degree. Then there exist cochain complexes $I_1^\bullet,I_2^\bullet,I_3^\bullet$ of injective objects of $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $I_k^n=0$ for $n<0$, morphisms of complexes $j:I_1^\bullet\to I_2^\bullet$, $q:I_2^\bullet\to I_3^\bullet$ such that $0\to I_1^n\xrightarrow{j^n}I_2^n\xrightarrow{q^n}I_3^n\to0$ is short exact for every $n$, and quasi-isomorphisms of complexes $\varphi_1:A^\bullet\to I_1^\bullet$, $\varphi_2:B^\bullet\to I_2^\bullet$, $\varphi_3:C^\bullet\to I_3^\bullet$ (morphisms of complexes inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology objects) with $\varphi_2\circ f=j\circ\varphi_1$ and $\varphi_3\circ g=q\circ\varphi_2$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses, line 6571), main assertion together with part (2) (if A^n = B^n = C^n = 0 for n < 0 one may take I_j^n = 0 for n < 0); injective resolutions of complexes in the sense of Section Tag 013G; proof Steps 1-2 (pushout along A -> I, then the termwise split case with I_2^n = I_1^n (+) I_3^n)

proof.text: **Step 1 (resolution of $A^\bullet$).** By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono] with $a=0$ applied to $A^\bullet$ there are a cochain complex $I_1^\bullet$ with injective terms and $I_1^n=0$ for $n<0$ and a quasi-isomorphism $\varphi_1:A^\bullet\to I_1^\bullet$. (That the $\varphi_1^n$ are monomorphisms is not needed.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses, line 6571), proof Step 1: 'Choose an injective resolution A -> I (see Lemma 013K)', with part (2) of 013T (bounded at 0)

proof.text: **Step 2 (pushout along $\varphi_1$).** The category of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ is abelian and a sequence of complexes is short exact in it if and only if it is short exact in each degree [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact]; so $0\to A^\bullet\xrightarrow{f}B^\bullet\xrightarrow{g}C^\bullet\to0$ is short exact in that category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] there with $u=\varphi_1$: we get a complex $E^\bullet$, morphisms of complexes $\iota:I_1^\bullet\to E^\bullet$, $v:B^\bullet\to E^\bullet$, $p:E^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ with $v\circ f=\iota\circ\varphi_1$, $p\circ v=g$, $p\circ\iota=0$, and $0\to I_1^\bullet\xrightarrow{\iota}E^\bullet\xrightarrow{p}C^\bullet\to0$ short exact, hence short exact in each degree [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact]. For $n<0$ the object $E^n$ sits in a short exact sequence $0\to I_1^n\to E^n\to C^n\to0$ with $I_1^n=C^n=0$, so $E^n=0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 1: 'Recall that Comp^+(A) is an abelian category, see Homology, Lemma 0114. Hence we may form the pushout along the map A -> I'

proof.text: **Step 3 ($v$ is a quasi-isomorphism).** Both rows $0\to A^\bullet\to B^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$ and $0\to I_1^\bullet\to E^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$ are short exact in each degree, so they have long exact cohomology sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], and since $(\varphi_1,v,\mathrm{id}_C)$ commutes with the maps of the rows ($v f=\iota\varphi_1$, $p v=g$) the maps $H^n(\varphi_1),H^n(v),H^n(\mathrm{id}_C)$ form a morphism of long exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality]. For each $n$ apply the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] to the segment $H^{n-1}(C^\bullet)\to H^n(A^\bullet)\to H^n(B^\bullet)\to H^n(C^\bullet)\to H^{n+1}(A^\bullet)$ mapping to $H^{n-1}(C^\bullet)\to H^n(I_1^\bullet)\to H^n(E^\bullet)\to H^n(C^\bullet)\to H^{n+1}(I_1^\bullet)$: the outer vertical maps $\mathrm{id}$, $H^n(\varphi_1)$, $\mathrm{id}$, $H^{n+1}(\varphi_1)$ are isomorphisms ($\varphi_1$ is a quasi-isomorphism), hence so is $H^n(v)$. Thus $v:B^\bullet\to E^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 1: 'Because of the 5-lemma and the last assertion of Homology, Lemma 0117 the map B -> E is a quasi-isomorphism'

proof.text: **Step 4 (the lower row is termwise split).** For every $n$ the sequence $0\to I_1^n\xrightarrow{\iota^n}E^n\xrightarrow{p^n}C^n\to0$ is short exact and $I_1^n$ is injective, so by [lem-weil-pbc-ses-injective-kernel-splits] there are $\pi^n:E^n\to I_1^n$ and $s^n:C^n\to E^n$ with $\pi^n\iota^n=\mathrm{id}$, $p^ns^n=\mathrm{id}$, $\iota^n\pi^n+s^np^n=\mathrm{id}_{E^n}$ (for $n<0$ all are $0$). From these identities also $\pi^ns^n=0$ (compose $\iota\pi s+sps=s$ with $\iota$ monic: $\iota\pi s=0$) and $p^n\iota^n=0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 1: 'Note that the lower short exact sequence is termwise split, see Homology, Lemma 0136. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma when 0 -> A -> B -> C -> 0 is termwise split'

proof.text: **Step 5 (the morphism $\delta$).** By [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-connecting-morphism] applied to $I_1^\bullet\xrightarrow{\iota}E^\bullet\xrightarrow{p}C^\bullet$ with the splittings of Step 4, the maps $\delta^n=\pi^{n+1}d_E^ns^n:C^n\to I_1^{n+1}$ form a morphism of complexes $\delta:C^\bullet\to I_1[1]^\bullet$, i.e. $d_{I_1}^{n+1}\delta^n+\delta^{n+1}d_C^n=0$. Moreover the differential of $E^\bullet$ is $d_E^n=\iota^{n+1}d_{I_1}^n\pi^n+\iota^{n+1}\delta^np^n+s^{n+1}d_C^np^n$: write $d_E^n=(\iota\pi+sp)\,d_E^n\,(\iota\pi+sp)$ and use $d_E\iota=\iota d_{I_1}$, $p\,d_E=d_Cp$ ($\iota$, $p$ are morphisms of complexes), $\pi\iota=\mathrm{id}$, $ps=\mathrm{id}$, $p\iota=0$; the four terms are $\iota d_{I_1}\pi$, $\iota\delta p$, $s\,d_C\,p\,\iota\,\pi=0$ and $s\,d_C\,p$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 2: 'Choose splittings. In other words, write B^n = A^n (+) C^n. Denote delta : C -> A[1] the morphism as in Homology, Lemma 011J'

proof.text: **Step 6 (resolution of $C^\bullet$).** By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono] with $a=0$ applied to $C^\bullet$ there are a complex $I_3^\bullet$ with injective terms and $I_3^n=0$ for $n<0$ and a quasi-isomorphism $f_3:C^\bullet\to I_3^\bullet$ with every $f_3^n$ a monomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 2: 'Choose injective resolutions f_1 : A -> I_1 and f_3 : C -> I_3 ... If A^n = C^n = 0 for n < 0, then pick these such that I_1^n = I_3^n = 0 for n < 0, see Lemma 013K ... We may assume f_3 is injective in every degree' (013K part (3))

proof.text: **Step 7 (lifting $\delta$).** The complex $I_1^\bullet$ already consists of injectives, so (as Stacks allows) we resolve it by itself, $f_1=\mathrm{id}$. The complex $I_1[1]^\bullet$ ($I_1[1]^n=I_1^{n+1}$, zero for $n<-1$) is bounded below with injective terms, $C^\bullet$ and $I_3^\bullet$ are bounded below, and $f_3$ is a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] with $\alpha=f_3$, $\gamma=\delta$ there is a morphism of complexes $\delta':I_3^\bullet\to I_1[1]^\bullet$ with $\delta'\circ f_3=\delta$; explicitly $\delta'^n:I_3^n\to I_1^{n+1}$ with $d_{I_1}^{n+1}\delta'^n+\delta'^{n+1}d_{I_3}^n=0$ and $\delta'^nf_3^n=\delta^n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 2: '(If A is a complex of injectives, then use I_1 = A.) ... By Lemma 013P we may find a morphism delta' : I_3 -> I_1[1] such that delta' o f_3 = f_1[1] o delta' (013P part (2))

proof.text: **Step 8 (the complex $I_2^\bullet$).** Put $I_2^n=I_1^n\oplus I_3^n$ with inclusions $j^n:I_1^n\to I_2^n$, $\epsilon^n:I_3^n\to I_2^n$ and projections $\mathrm{pr}^n:I_2^n\to I_1^n$, $q^n:I_2^n\to I_3^n$, and $d_{I_2}^n=\begin{pmatrix}d_{I_1}^n&\delta'^n\\0&d_{I_3}^n\end{pmatrix}$, i.e. $d_{I_2}^n=j\,d_{I_1}\mathrm{pr}+j\,\delta'q+\epsilon\,d_{I_3}q$. Then $d_{I_2}^{n+1}d_{I_2}^n=\begin{pmatrix}d_{I_1}d_{I_1}&d_{I_1}\delta'+\delta'd_{I_3}\\0&d_{I_3}d_{I_3}\end{pmatrix}=0$ by Step 7, so $I_2^\bullet$ is a complex; $I_2^n=0$ for $n<0$; $I_2^n$, a product of two injectives, is injective [lem-weil-pbc-product-injectives]. The first column and the second row of the matrix give $d_{I_2}j=j\,d_{I_1}$ and $q\,d_{I_2}=d_{I_3}q$, so $j:I_1^\bullet\to I_2^\bullet$ and $q:I_2^\bullet\to I_3^\bullet$ are morphisms of complexes, and $0\to I_1^n\xrightarrow{j^n}I_2^n\xrightarrow{q^n}I_3^n\to0$ is (split) short exact for every $n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 2: 'Set I_2^n = I_1^n (+) I_3^n. Define d_{I_2}^n = ((d_{I_1}^n, (delta')^n), (0, d_{I_3}^n))'

proof.text: **Step 9 (the morphism $\psi:E^\bullet\to I_2^\bullet$).** Define $\psi^n=j^n\pi^n+\epsilon^nf_3^np^n:E^n\to I_2^n$ (the sum of $\mathrm{id}_{I_1^n}$ and $f_3^n$ in the splitting $E^n=I_1^n\oplus C^n$). By Step 5 and $\pi\iota=\mathrm{id}$, $\pi s=0$, $p\iota=0$, $ps=\mathrm{id}$: $\psi^{n+1}d_E^n=j(d_{I_1}\pi+\delta p)+\epsilon f_3d_Cp$, while $d_{I_2}\psi^n=j(d_{I_1}\pi+\delta'f_3p)+\epsilon d_{I_3}f_3p$; these agree since $\delta'f_3=\delta$ (Step 7) and $d_{I_3}f_3=f_3d_C$. So $\psi$ is a morphism of complexes, with $\psi\circ\iota=j$ and $q\circ\psi=f_3\circ p$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 2: 'define the maps B^n -> I_2^n to be given as the sum of the maps A^n -> I_1^n and C^n -> I_3^n. Everything is clear.'

proof.text: **Step 10 ($\psi$ is a quasi-isomorphism).** $(\mathrm{id}_{I_1},\psi,f_3)$ is a morphism from the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to I_1^\bullet\to E^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$ to $0\to I_1^\bullet\xrightarrow{j}I_2^\bullet\xrightarrow{q}I_3^\bullet\to0$ (Step 9). Their long exact cohomology sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] are related by the maps $H^n(\mathrm{id}),H^n(\psi),H^n(f_3)$ [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality], and the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] on $H^{n-1}(C^\bullet)\to H^n(I_1^\bullet)\to H^n(E^\bullet)\to H^n(C^\bullet)\to H^{n+1}(I_1^\bullet)$, with outer vertical maps $H^{n-1}(f_3)$, $\mathrm{id}$, $H^n(f_3)$, $\mathrm{id}$ isomorphisms, shows that $H^n(\psi)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 2, 'Everything is clear' (that B -> I_2 is a quasi-isomorphism), written out with Homology Lemma Tag 0117 and the 5-lemma Tag 05QB as in Step 1

proof.text: **Step 11 (conclusion).** Put $\varphi_2=\psi\circ v:B^\bullet\to I_2^\bullet$ and $\varphi_3=f_3$. Then $\varphi_2$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $H^n(\varphi_2)=H^n(\psi)H^n(v)$ being a composite of isomorphisms (Steps 3, 10); $\varphi_2\circ f=\psi v f=\psi\iota\varphi_1=j\circ\varphi_1$ (Steps 2, 9) and $q\circ\varphi_2=q\psi v=f_3pv=f_3g=\varphi_3\circ g$. The complexes $I_1^\bullet,I_2^\bullet,I_3^\bullet$ have injective terms and vanish in negative degrees (Steps 1, 6, 8), and $0\to I_1^n\to I_2^n\to I_3^n\to0$ is short exact for every $n$ (Step 8).

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof, end of Step 2 combined with the reduction of Step 1

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Eleven steps along Steps 1-2 of the proof of 013T with its part (2); five new nodes: three Mathlib leaves verified by line (0136 (1)=>(3): ShortExact.splittingOfInjective, ShortComplex/ShortExact.lean:205; 011J: CochainComplex.homOfDegreewiseSplit, DegreewiseSplit.lean:63 with homOfDegreewiseSplit_f :68; 013P(2) for bounded-below complexes: the lifting-property instance of the injective model structure, ModelCategory/Injective.lean:160, a specialization through the translation lemmas, accepted) and two unsplit (013K(3) resolution by a degreewise monomorphism; the pushout of a short exact sequence along a morphism, Homology 010I item (2)). The argument: resolve A, push out along phi_1 (v a quasi-isomorphism by the long exact sequences, naturality and the five lemma), split the lower row termwise, build delta: C -> I_1[1] and the matrix form of d_E, resolve C by a degreewise mono quasi-isomorphism f_3, lift delta along f_3, form I_2 = I_1 (+) I_3 with the twisted differential, psi: E -> I_2 a quasi-isomorphism by the five lemma again, phi_2 = psi v. Steps 9 and 11 are elementary identities from the splitting relations, checked. Noted for stage 3: the object version lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses asserts its second pushout is I_A^0 (+) I_C^0 without a reason and could be re-split as this lemma applied to A[0], B[0], C[0].

Wrote the proof in 11 steps following 013T Steps 1-2: resolve A (013K(3)), push out along A -> I_1 in the abelian category of complexes, quasi-isomorphism by the long exact sequence and the five lemma, termwise splitting (0136), delta : C -> I_1[1] (011J), resolve C degreewise-monomorphically (013K(3)), lift delta along f_3 (013P(2)), build I_2 = I_1 (+) I_3 with the twisted differential, the comparison E -> I_2 and its quasi-isomorphism, and compose. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono (013K(3), unsplit; Mathlib has only the mono version one degree lower or the non-mono version), lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence (Homology 010I(2)/08N4/08N3, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-ses-injective-kernel-splits (0136, Mathlib ShortExact.splittingOfInjective), lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-connecting-morphism (011J, Mathlib CochainComplex.homOfDegreewiseSplit), lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso (013P(2) for bounded below complexes, Mathlib lifting instance of the Quillen model structure on CochainComplex.Plus). lean.statement: theorem exists_injective_resolution_ses_complexes {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives C] (A B D : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D) (hA : ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (A.X n)) (hB : ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (B.X n)) (hD : ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (D.X n)) (hSES : ∃ hfg : f ≫ g = 0, ∀ n : ℤ, ((ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).map (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).ShortExact) : ∃ (I₁ I₂ I₃ : CochainComplex C ℤ) (j : I₁ ⟶ I₂) (q : I₂ ⟶ I₃) (φ₁ : A ⟶ I₁) (φ₂ : B ⟶ I₂) (φ₃ : D ⟶ I₃), (∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (I₁.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (I₂.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (I₃.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Injective (I₁.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Injective (I₂.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Injective (I₃.X n)) ∧ (∃ hjq : j ≫ q = 0, ∀ n : ℤ, ((ShortComplex.mk j q hjq).map (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).ShortExact) ∧ QuasiIso φ₁ ∧ QuasiIso φ₂ ∧ QuasiIso φ₃ ∧ f ≫ φ₂ = φ₁ ≫ j ∧ g ≫ φ₃ = φ₂ ≫ q
